Chandra, learned counsel for respondent nos. 3 to 5 and Sri Rajiv Gupta,
learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for State-respondents. 
2. Petitioner is aggrieved by order dated 19.07.2023 passed by respondent
No. 4 deciding the dispute relating to carry forward of dues of the alleged
erstwhile tenant of the premises owned by the petitioner as well as dispute
relating to release of new connection. 
20→3. The finding recorded in the impugned order is that one Mohan Lal was the
tenant of the petitioner and there were dues outstanding against him. The
same is to be paid before any new connection could be granted. 
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the dues are for a period
more than two years old and, therefore, it cannot be recovered in view of
Section 56 of the Act. In support of his contention, he has placed reliance on a
judgement of Supreme Court in the case of Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam
Limited V. Rahamatullah Khan, (2020) 4 SCC 650. 
5. Sri Udit Chandra, learned counsel appearing for respondents Electricity
Department submits that the dispute in question falls squarely within the
30→purview of Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, under Clause 7.10 of the

U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He submits that since factual issues have
been raised in the instant petition and, therefore, the petitioner should be
relegated to the statutory remedy available under the Code 2005. 
6. Clause 7.10 (ii) & (iii) stipulates that any consumer aggrieved by any
action of the Licensee, in respect of the matters mentioned in clauses 7.7.1 to
7.7.5 or those covered under the said Regulations may file a complaint with
the Licensee. If the licensee fails to settle the complaint of the consumer
within the time limits specified in the Code or otherwise provided in the
40→Regulations, or the consumer is not satisfied by the decision of the licensee,
the consumer may file a complaint in the Consumer Grievance Redressal
Forum as per the specified procedure under the said Regulations. He submits
that the dispute relating to carrying forward of the dues of the erstwhile
tenant is a billing dispute covered under Clause 7.7.4 of the Code and the
dispute relating to dues and new connection is covered by Clause 7.7.2 of the
Code. He further submits that the judgement in Rahamatullah Khan has
been distinguished by the Supreme Court in a latter judgement by Three
Judges Bench in the case of K.C. Ninan Vs. Kerala State Electricity Board &
Ors., 2023 SCC Online SC 663. He further submits that in any case, the
50→aforesaid plea can also be raised by the petitioner before the Consumer
Grievance Redressal Forum. 
7. Having considered the rival submissions, we are satisfied that the
petitioner has alternative efficacious remedy of approaching the Consumer
Grievance Redressal Forum and, therefore, we decline to examine the
challenge and leave it open to the petitioner to avail remedy provided under
the Code. 
8. It is also provided that in case the petitioner approaches the Consumer
Grievance Redressal Forum, for redressal of his grievance, the Forum will
decide the same expeditiously preferably within twelve weeks from the date
60→complaint is filed before it. 
9. The petition stands disposed of accordingly."

this writ petition, the following prayers :- 

"i. to issue a writ order or direction in the nature of certiorari to
quash the order dated 19.7.2023 passed by Respondent no.4
through Letter No.2821/N.V.V. Kh-II, Va (As Annexure no.13 of

ii. to issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus
70→directing the respondents to issue a commercial electricity

iii. to issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondent no.4 not to recover Electricity dues of
Mohan Lal from the petitioner and also not shift (sic.) the
Electricity dues of Mohan Lal upon the petitioner house." 
3. From the prayers, we find that the very same order dated
19.7.2023, which was challenged in Writ-C No.37208 of 2023, is
being challenged in this writ petition also. 
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner, relying upon the news item at
80→page 31 of the writ petition, has stated before the Court that the
Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum in Varanasi is not
functioning. 
5. Learned counsel appearing for the Electricity Department,
however, has submitted that the Consumer Grievance Redressal
Forum in Varanasi is definitely functioning. 
6. From the records and the averments made in the writ petition it

Court by means of the instant writ petition is that the application
under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 when
90→was not being decided, the grievance of the petitioner be looked

counsel appearing for the Electricity Department to enquire as to
